value.behaviour: Documents backstage.io/former-names: format, claim rules, conflict behaviour and permissions.
rules: 1. Section heading '### backstage.io/former-names' followed by a YAML example: metadata.name new-service with annotation backstage.io/former-names: 'old-service, legacy/older-service'.

2. Format: a comma-separated list of entity refs; whitespace around items is ignored; a short form (name or namespace/name) takes the entity's own kind and namespace; refs are compared case-insensitively.

3. Claim rules as a list: a former ref must have the same kind as the entity; it must not be the entity's own current ref; it must follow the usual naming rules; a ref in another namespace is allowed. An invalid item is reported as a processing error on the entity that names the item.

4. Behaviour: opening the entity page or TechDocs URL of a former ref redirects to the entity's current URL and shows a notice that the entity was renamed. A live entity always keeps its own name, so if an entity currently holds the ref there is no redirect. If more than one entity claims the same former ref, there is no redirect and the catalog logs a warning.
5. Permissions: the redirect only happens when the user may read the entity that claims the ref; otherwise the page shows Entity not found, the same as when nothing claims the ref.
6. Mention the catalog endpoint GET /entities/by-former-name/<kind>/<namespace>/<name> with a link to api.md.

Note that refs held by other entities, such as spec.owner, are not rewritten and must be updated by hand.

rules: 1. Front matter `'@backstage/catalog-model': minor`.

2. Text: Added the `backstage.io/former-names` well-known annotation (`ANNOTATION_FORMER_NAMES`) and the `parseFormerEntityRefs` helper. Entities can list the refs they were previously known by, and the default entity validation reports invalid items, such as a former ref of a different kind or the entity's own ref, as processing errors.
1. Front matter `'@backstage/catalog-client': minor`.

2. Text: Added the optional `getEntityRefByFormerRef` method to `CatalogApi`, implemented by `CatalogClient` and `InMemoryCatalogClient`. It resolves a former entity ref, as declared with the `backstage.io/former-names` annotation, to the current ref of the renamed entity, or `undefined` when there is no unambiguous match.
1. Front matter `'@backstage/plugin-catalog-backend': minor`.

2. Text: The catalog now indexes the refs listed in the `backstage.io/former-names` annotation and adds the `GET /entities/by-former-name/:kind/:namespace/:name` endpoint, which returns the current ref of the entity that claims a former ref. It responds with 404 when a live entity holds the ref, when nothing claims it, when several entities claim it (a warning is logged), or when the caller may not read the claimant. Existing lookups are unchanged and no database migration is needed.
1. Front matter `'@backstage/plugin-catalog': minor`.

2. Text: When an entity page URL does not match any entity, the page now checks whether a renamed entity lists that ref in its `backstage.io/former-names` annotation. If so, it redirects to the entity's current URL, keeping the selected tab and query parameters, and shows a notice that the entity was renamed. This works in both the old and the new frontend system, and normal page loads make no extra request.
1. Front matter `'@backstage/plugin-techdocs': minor`.

2. Text: The TechDocs reader now redirects links for an entity that was renamed to the docs of its current ref, when the entity lists its old ref in the `backstage.io/former-names` annotation. The page path within the docs, the query string and the anchor are kept, and the reader shows a notice that the entity was renamed. This works in both the old and the new frontend system.
